title: From Rammed Earth to Bricks: The Great Wall's Epic Building Story
title_zh: 从夯土到砖石：长城的史诗建造故事
intro_zh: 本文实际目标词数约950词，共9段。围绕长城的历史与建造展开，介绍了从春秋战国到明朝的修建过程、材料技术、烽火台系统及其文化意义。重点掌握约6个核心词汇，理解难度适中。

paragraphs.en: The Great Wall of China is often called the 'longest wall in the world.' In fact, it is not a single wall but a complex system of fortifications, including walls, watchtowers, and barriers. According to a 2012 national survey, all sections of the wall add up to more than 21,000 kilometers. That distance equals about half the circumference of the Earth. For over two thousand years, these structures protected Chinese civilization from invasions from the north. But how did ancient builders manage to build such a huge project without modern machines? The answer is a combination of human will, simple tools, and clever engineering.
paragraphs.zh: 中国长城常被称为“世界上最长的墙”。事实上，它不是一道单一的墙，而是一个复杂的防御工事系统，包括城墙、瞭望塔和屏障。根据2012年全国调查，长城所有部分加起来超过21000公里。这个距离相当于地球周长的一半。两千多年来，这些建筑保护了中华文明免受北方入侵。但是，古代工匠在没有现代机器的情况下是如何建造如此巨大的工程的呢？答案是人的意志、简单工具和巧妙工程的结合。

paragraphs.en: The earliest defensive walls appeared during the Spring and Autumn Period (770-476 BCE), when rival kingdoms fought each other. Each kingdom built earthen barriers to guard its own territory. These walls were typically only two or three meters high, but they marked boundaries and slowed down enemy soldiers. Later, during the Warring States Period, kingdoms built even longer walls along their borders. However, it was Emperor Qin Shi Huang who first united China in 221 BCE and ordered the northern walls to be connected and extended. This massive project created the initial version of the Great Wall.
paragraphs.zh: 最早的防御城墙出现在春秋时期（公元前770-476年），当时各国相互争斗。各诸侯国修建土墙来守卫自己的领土。这些墙通常只有两三米高，但可以标记边界并减缓敌军速度。后来，在战国时期，各国在边界修建了更长的墙。然而，是秦始皇在公元前221年首次统一中国，并下令连接和延伸北方的城墙。这个庞大的工程创造了长城的初始版本。

paragraphs.en: Building the Qin-era wall was a nightmare for the workers. Historical records say that around 300,000 soldiers, peasants, and prisoners were forced to labor on the project. They worked in extreme weather, from bitter cold winters to scorching summers. Many died from exhaustion, hunger, or accidents. Some were buried inside the wall, giving rise to the saying that the Great Wall is the 'longest cemetery in the world.' The main construction method was rammed earth. Workers built wooden frames, filled them with soil, and pounded the earth tightly with heavy tools. This produced walls that were surprisingly solid.
paragraphs.zh: 修建秦代长城对工人来说是一场噩梦。历史记载约有30万士兵、农民和囚犯被迫在工地上劳动。他们在极端天气中工作，从严寒的冬天到酷热的夏天。许多人死于劳累、饥饿或事故。有些人被埋在城墙里，因此有了“长城是世界上最长的墓地”的说法。主要的建造方法是夯土。工人搭建木框架，填入土壤，用重工具将泥土夯紧。这样可以造出非常坚固的墙。

paragraphs.en: Many later dynasties repaired or expanded the Great Wall. The Han Dynasty (206 BCE–220 CE) extended it westward to protect the Silk Road trade routes. Historians estimate that the Han built an additional 10,000 kilometers of wall in the northern frontier. During the Northern Wei and Northern Qi dynasties, rulers ordered small sections to be built in northern China. The Sui Dynasty also used forced labor to repair walls. However, the most famous and impressive sections were constructed during the Ming Dynasty, which lasted from 1368 to 1644. Ming emperors feared invasion from the northern tribes, so they made the wall a top national priority.
paragraphs.zh: 许多后代朝代修缮或扩建了长城。汉朝（公元前206-公元220年）向西延伸以保护丝绸之路的贸易路线。历史学家估计汉朝在北方边疆增建了约1万公里的城墙。在北魏和北齐时期，统治者下令在中国北方修建小段城墙。隋朝也使用强迫劳动修缮城墙。然而，最著名和最壮观的段落是在明朝（1368-1644年）建造的。明朝皇帝害怕北方部落入侵，因此将长城列为国家头等大事。

paragraphs.en: The Ming Dynasty transformed the building materials and design. The earlier rammed-earth walls were gradually replaced by walls with a core of earth and stones and outer layers of durable bricks and large stone slabs. These bricks were made in local workshops and fired at high temperatures. Each brick weighed about 15 kilograms, and workers needed to carry them up steep mountains. They used hand tools like hammers, chisels, and ropes. To keep the structure tight, they poured sticky rice soup mixed with lime into the gaps. This special mixture made the wall extremely strong and long-lasting.
paragraphs.zh: 明朝改变了建筑材料和设计。早期的夯土墙逐渐被替换为土石核心、外层是耐用的砖块和巨大石板条砌成的墙。这些砖在当地的作坊里高温烧制而成。每块砖重约15公斤，工人需要把它们搬上陡峭的山。他们使用锤子、凿子和绳子等手工具。为了使结构紧密，他们向缝隙中倒入糯米汤和石灰的混合物。这种特殊的混合物使城墙非常坚固且持久。

paragraphs.en: One of the cleverest features of the Ming wall was the beacon tower system. Towers were placed about 10 kilometers (or 10 li) apart on the high ground. When enemy troops were spotted, soldiers lit fires to send signals. Different numbers of fires indicated different enemy troop sizes. For example, one fire and one cannon shot meant that fewer than 100 enemies were approaching, while two fires meant more than 500. There were also other signals such as flags and smoke. This early warning system allowed garrisons along the wall to prepare for battle quickly. It was like an ancient communication network.
paragraphs.zh: 明长城最巧妙的特点之一是烽火塔系统。塔建在高地上，彼此相隔约10公里（或10里）。当发现敌军时，士兵点燃火来发送信号。火的数量不同表示敌军规模不同。例如，一处火和一声炮响表示敌人少于100人，两处火表示超过500人。还有旗帜和烟雾等其他信号。这个预警系统使沿墙的驻军能够迅速准备战斗。它就像古代的通讯网络。

paragraphs.en: The Great Wall served a purpose beyond military defense. It controlled the movement of people and goods. In the Ming Dynasty, officials set up gates and checkpoints along the wall. Traders had to show documentation and pay taxes. The wall also provided a convenient road for transporting supplies. In addition, the wall symbolized the power and unity of the empire. Every year, the emperor sent officials to inspect the walls and care for the garrisons. Soldiers stationed there received rewards and supplies. Over time, the wall became a barrier that separated farming areas from nomadic regions, shaping the way of life on both sides.
paragraphs.zh: 长城不仅仅用于军事防御。它控制人员和货物的流动。在明代，官员沿墙设置关口和检查站。商人必须出示证件并纳税。长城还为运送物资提供了便利的通道。此外，长城象征着帝国的力量和统一。每年，皇帝派官员视察城墙并照顾驻军。驻守在那里的士兵获得奖励和补给。随着时间的推移，长城成为分隔农耕区和游牧区的屏障，塑造了两侧的生活方式。

paragraphs.en: Today, the Great Wall is more than a relic. It is a UNESCO World Heritage site and a symbol of Chinese national pride. Each year, millions of tourists visit restored sections such as Badaling and Mutianyu near Beijing. Some adventurous travelers hike the wild sections where the wall is crumbling. However, preserving the wall is a huge challenge. It is estimated that about 30 percent of the Ming wall has disappeared due to natural erosion and human damage. In recent years, the Chinese government has spent millions of dollars on restoration. Modern engineers are learning from ancient techniques, such as using rammed earth and lime to repair and protect the structure.
paragraphs.zh: 今天，长城不仅仅是一个遗迹。它是联合国教科文组织世界遗产，也是中华民族自豪的象征。每年，数百万游客参观北京附近的八达岭和慕田峪等修复段落。一些喜欢冒险的旅行者会在坍塌的野长城上徒步。然而，保护长城是一项巨大挑战。据估计，约30%的明长城因自然侵蚀和人为破坏已经消失。近年来，中国政府已投入数百万美元用于修复。现代工程师正在学习古代技术，例如使用夯土和石灰来修复和保护结构。

paragraphs.en: The Great Wall is not just a wall; it is a monument to human endurance. It shows what people can achieve with limited resources and unlimited determination. Despite the cost in human lives, its construction aimed at peace and protection. Today, we can still climb its steps and feel the history beneath our feet. As we look across the winding walls, we remember the countless hands that built them. The Great Wall tells us that great things can be created when people work together, even under the most difficult conditions.
paragraphs.zh: 长城不仅仅是一堵墙；它是人类忍耐力的纪念碑。它展示了人们在有限资源和无限决心下能取得的成就。尽管付出了生命的代价，它的建造旨在和平与保护。今天，我们仍可以爬上它的台阶，感受脚下的历史。当我们眺望蜿蜒的城墙，我们想起建造它们的无数双手。长城告诉我们，当人们共同工作时，即使在最艰难的条件下，也能创造出伟大的事物。

questions.q: What is the main idea of this passage?
options: The Great Wall was built by different dynasties with different materials.
The Great Wall is a symbol of China and a popular tourist destination.
The passage mainly focuses on the history and construction methods of the Great Wall.
The Great Wall was only used for military defense.
questions.explain: 文章从多个朝代讲述长城的修建历史，并详细说明了建造技术、材料和功能，因此主旨是“长城的历史与建造方法”。A不全面，B是现状，D错误，因为还有贸易等非军事功能。

questions.q: According to the passage, which dynasty used bricks and stones to build the wall?
questions.explain: 原文第五段明确提到“The Ming Dynasty transformed the building materials and design... outer layers of durable bricks and large stone slabs”，所以是明代。

questions.q: The word 'durable' in paragraph 5 most nearly means ______.
questions.explain: “durable”意为耐用的、持久的，与long-lasting同义。文中说外层是durable bricks，强调坚固持久。

questions.q: What can be inferred about the building of the Great Wall from the passage?
options: It was easy to build because of good weather.
It required thousands of workers but not much time.
It was a difficult project that cost many lives.
It was built quickly by using advanced machines.
questions.explain: 第三段描述工人被迫劳动，许多人死于劳累、饥饿或事故，有些人被埋在墙下，因此可推断修建工程难度巨大且付出大量生命代价。其他选项与原文相悖。
